title: What Are the Japanese Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget

refresh_of.note: Person: article to refresh. Publish method: update in place, change slug and path to /expert-advice/japanese-wedding-traditions, confirm the old URL returns a 301. Check for duplicate Japanese pages. Protect its rankings.

notes: REFRESH: the brief reads the old page with mcp__Apify__apify--web-fetch (one render-wait retry if the body is empty; if the call is DECLINED, do not retry and infer coverage from rankings). SEO pulls its ranked keywords (US and AU), checks duplicates, and the outline keeps covering every query with real volume. Never reuse wording; drop errors.

AUTHORITY RULE (content-system/brand/voice-guide.md 'Write with authority'): no research talk in the copy (what we could or couldn't find, trace or confirm; our sources or method; what the internet says; myths sections; 'you will often read'). Customs without a strong source are written as living practice in a confident voice ('In many Japanese families...'), never with a meaning or origin stated as fact. 'Often told' at most once per post, never 'it is often told that'. No hedge stacking: cite a source once by link; date legal and travel facts once per section. Source gaps go in the run report only.
Customs vary by family and region, and between Shinto, chapel and civil-only weddings; say so once. Japanese terms with macrons as sources give them (yuinō, hirōen, goshūgi).

Likely customs (brief finalises): yuinō (betrothal gift exchange, no amounts); the Shinto ceremony (shinzen shiki) and san-san-kudo; dress (shiromuku, wataboshi or tsunokakushi, iro-uchikake); Christian-style chapel weddings as sources describe them; the reception (hirōen) and oiro-naoshi; goshūgi (no amounts) and hikidemono; kagami biraki; speeches and the bride's letter to her parents; senbazuru as living practice.
UNESCO only where its own text links an element to weddings (for example washoku, 2013, if its text names weddings). Confirm each page live and its title.

Destination angle: Smartraveller Japan checked live (overall level and any higher-level areas; risks as Smartraveller words them). Legal from official sources only: Australian Embassy Tokyo and consulates (CNI or affidavit, notarial), Smartraveller 'Getting married overseas' (recognition), municipal office (kuyakusho/shiyakusho) registration only if an official page can be read; otherwise questions to ask the municipal office and the embassy, including any fees; 'as at November 2026'. A shrine or chapel ceremony not replacing registration only if an official source says so. Kyoto, Tokyo and Hakone named only as places couples choose; shrines named only as places, never as venues. Japanese-Australian weddings at home.

Sources: japan.travel (JNTO), Jinja Honcho and shrine pages, Tokyo National Museum, Kyoto Costume Institute, V&A, UNESCO, Britannica, academic sources. Never competitor wedding sites, vendor blogs or Wikipedia.

Links: Asia destination pages from the link map, related traditions drafts (Chinese, Indonesian), /wonderland-concierge, /magazine. UTMs: utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=japanese-wedding-traditions&utm_content=primary|secondary.

Images: placeholders only; no AI images of people, cultural dress, ceremonies or places; AI only for neutral still lifes (sake cups, paper cranes) labelled illustrative pending approval; old-page images only if licence confirmed.

Speed: WebFetch cannot reach outside sites; Apify web-fetch (parallel) and DataForSEO from the start. Fact-check as 2 parallel batches (A: yuinō, Shinto ceremony, dress, chapel weddings; B: reception, gifts, kagami biraki, speeches, cranes, UNESCO and legal), 15 min HARD by the clock, save after every 3 facts, separate scratch folders; self_qa.confidence must be a number; must_include_coverage entries must be objects with covered_by as an array; no extra sourcing rounds; never retry a declined call. Stop at the limit: start no new reads after 15 minutes.
Headings must not contain pasted keywords in brackets.

Do not use 'from first idea to the last dance' or 'last dance'; Advisor claims only from brand-facts.md (single point of contact; fee and inclusions in writing); no implied help with legal or church paperwork.
Person's standards: exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways; no prices or amounts; no vendor or venue names; business details deferred; Australian English; no em dashes.
